references.text: God presents himself to Moses as 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' – the direct Old Testament quotation that Jesus builds his argument on in Luke 20:37-38. That God calls himself the God of the deceased patriarchs shows that they live for him.

The Lord confirms again to Moses that he is 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' and that this is his name forever (Exodus 3:15). This underscores the enduring relationship between God and the patriarchs.
Moses refers to God as 'the living God' (Deuteronomy 5:26). God is the God of the living, not the dead, which aligns with Jesus' point in Luke 20:38.
'For with you is the fountain of life' (Psalm 36:10). God is the source of all life, and all live for him, as Jesus states.
Isaiah prophesies about the resurrection: 'Your dead shall live; my dead bodies shall arise' (Isaiah 26:19). This points to the same hope of resurrection that Jesus defends before the Sadducees.

Daniel prophesies that 'many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake' (Daniel 12:2-3). The hope of resurrection in the Old Testament supports Jesus' argument that the dead live for God.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. He is not the God of the dead, but of the living' (Matthew 22:32).
The parallel passage in Mark: 'He is not God of the dead, but of the living' (Mark 12:27). Mark adds, 'You are greatly mistaken,' which underscores the seriousness of the Sadducees' error.
Paul writes that Christ, raised from the dead, dies no more – 'the life he lives, he lives to God' (Romans 6:10-11). Living for God is at the heart of resurrection life, in line with Jesus' words.

'Whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord. For Christ died and came to life again so that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living' (Romans 14:8-9). All live for God, whether in life or death.
Paul writes: 'I live for God … it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me' (Galatians 2:19-20). Living for God is central to the Christian faith, extending Jesus' words that all live for him.
Paul calls God 'the living God' (1 Timothy 4:10), who is the Savior of all people. God's attribute as the living one underscores that he is the God of the living, not the dead.
